nodes.title: Gate the root before walking
nodes.why: A matching root removes the whole tree, so checking it first returns the empty string without any traversal.
nodes.alternative: Treat the root like a child inside the walk and special-case the output.
nodes.tradeoff: One extra line, but the contract for a matching root is explicit.

nodes.title: Turn depth into indentation
nodes.why: Carrying a depth counter means the output line is computed at visit time; no second pass over the tree is needed.
nodes.alternative: Build nested arrays first and flatten them with indentation later.
nodes.tradeoff: Simple and linear, though the depth must be threaded through every recursive call.

nodes.title: Skip a matching child and its subtree
nodes.why: Skipping the recursive call drops the entire subtree in one decision, which is the required semantics.
nodes.alternative: Filter children into a new array before recursing.
nodes.tradeoff: Avoids allocating filtered arrays, but the prune rule lives inside the loop body.

nodes.title: Join collected lines once
nodes.why: Collecting lines in an array and joining once avoids a trailing newline and repeated string concatenation.
nodes.alternative: Append to a string with a newline after every node.
nodes.tradeoff: Cleaner output contract at the cost of one array.

nodes.title: Keep traversal state on an explicit stack
nodes.why: Frames of node and depth replace the call stack, so very deep trees cannot overflow it.
nodes.alternative: Recurse and rely on the engine's call stack.
nodes.tradeoff: More code, but no recursion limit and a visible traversal order.

nodes.title: Push children in reverse to keep sibling order
nodes.why: A stack pops the last pushed frame first, so pushing the last child first makes the first child come out next.
nodes.alternative: Use a queue, which would turn the walk into breadth-first order.
nodes.tradeoff: A reverse loop is slightly unusual to read but preserves the required depth-first order.

nodes.title: Apply the prune gate while pushing
nodes.why: A matching child is never pushed, so neither it nor its subtree is ever visited.
nodes.alternative: Push every child and check the gate after popping.
nodes.tradeoff: Fewer frames on the stack; the gate is evaluated once per child either way.

nodes.title: Join collected lines once
nodes.why: The output contract has no trailing newline, which a single join guarantees.
nodes.tradeoff: One array allocation for a clean contract.
